context: Merge PR #18 and its accepted follow-ups first. Run gate 1, the acceptance harness with --require against a real hosted database, and gate 2, one real downstream consumer command, before tagging; record both in the release PR body per the release-gates evidence rules. Bump the version and lockfile, finalize the changelog, build and verify artifacts, and publish. Then upgrade BenchBox and confirm an ordinary tracker command succeeds in a session that was not specially prepared, which is the acceptance criterion this whole sequence exists to satisfy. Do not add authentication logic to the Pi adapter or to any consumer wrapper.
description: Downstream consumers still run v0.4.2, in which hosted authentication is unusable without a manually exported token. The credential provider, its provisioning procedure, the acceptance harness, and the release gates all land in PR #18 but reach no consumer until a release is cut. BenchBox's v0.4.2 upgrade was completed and then failed on first use with E_AUTH_MISSING; that upgrade needs re-running against a release that actually works, with no BenchBox-specific or Pi-specific authentication logic, because the whole point is that every caller uses the same resolver through the same wrapper. This release is auth-affecting by definition, so docs/operations/release-gates.md applies in full: both gates run before the tag, and a failed gate blocks it.

anti_patterns.dont: Add credential handling to the Pi adapter or a consumer wrapper to make the upgrade succeed
anti_patterns.instead: fix the resolver or the provisioning procedure
anti_patterns.why: consumer-specific authentication logic is the failure this architecture removed and would hide a resolver defect

anti_patterns.dont: Satisfy the release gates with green CI, passing tests, and verified checksums
anti_patterns.instead: run the harness against a real database and one real consumer command
anti_patterns.why: all of those held for v0.4.2 while the release was unusable

anti_patterns.dont: Tag the release and then upgrade the consumer to see whether it works
anti_patterns.instead: run the downstream check before the tag
anti_patterns.why: that is the exact sequence that put a broken v0.4.2 into BenchBox before anyone could stop it

preserves.behavior: Both release gates run before the tag; a failed gate blocks the release rather than becoming a follow-up.
No authentication logic is added to the Pi adapter, the BenchBox wrapper, or any other consumer.
No credential value, hosted URL, or consumer secret is recorded as release evidence.
The v2 wrapper contract and ADR 0004 credential lifecycle are unchanged by the release.

verifications.command: uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .

verifications.description: Gate 1 passes against a real hosted database
